caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 27 of 2002
lawyer:
AKM Nazrul  Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Sharif uddin Chaklader; Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners. 
KZ Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain. Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 1.
Not Represented ----- Respondent Nos. 2-9.
parties:
Shishir Kanti Pal and others  ----- Petitioners 
Vs.
Nur Muhammad and others  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
12. The leave petition has been filed by the heirs of non-contesting defendant Nos. 7 and 8 (petitioner Nos. 1-5) the non-contesting defendant Nos. 10-12, non-contesting subsequent transferees (petitioner Nos. 10-12) and the contesting defendant No.5. The learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that Exhibit 1-irrevocable power of attorney in the form of deed of exchange-is a spurious document and that the said Exhibit 1 cannot be treated as a document of title creating interest in the immovable property and that this fact has not been noticed by the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court and thus has caused failure of justice, that the irrevocable power of attorney as was not endorsed by the then Pakistan High Commission of India and, as such, no credence as could be given to that both High Court Division and the Court of appeal below erred in treating power of attorney as the basis of right, that the High Court Division has affirmed the judgment of the Court of appeal below upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court without considering the total materials on record and that the appellate Court arrived at the erroneous decision upon the wrong presumption on a false and forged power of attorney which is not a document of title and that fact of execution and due authentication and registration having not been duly established, that from the plaintiffs' side no material has been placed on record as to why the Exhibit 1 was revalidated and re-stamped in the Office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Comilla while the property in schedule 'A' which plaintiffs claim to have got on the basis of their exchange of the property described in schedule 'B' in the Tripura State, India is undisputedly the properties situate in the District of Noakhali, that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court wrongly shifted the onus upon the defendants relating to revalidation and re-stamping of the Exhibit 1 in Comilla, that High Court Division as well as appellate Court were in error in drawing up the presumption of genuineness, of Exhibit 1 on the finding that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land although plaintiffs in support of their claim of possession have examined solitary witness PW 2, that High Court Division as well as the court of appeal below were in error in holding that Exhibit 1 was authenticated by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla although there is no reference in Exhibit 1 of any case number in initiation where of the document was revalidated and re-stamped, that High Court Division as well as the court of appeal below were in serious error in holding that the plaintiffs are in possession of the 'A' scheduled land for long 30 years on the basis of Exhibit 1. 

 16. The contention of the defendant No.5 was that plaintiffs used to go from Noakhali to Tripura State and that used to work there as seasonal labour and as such the question of their having land as described in schedule 'B' in the Tripura State was a myth. This contention of the defendant No.5 has not been established by placing any material on record. The plaintiffs are claiming the land on the basis of Exhibit 1. Fact of plaintiffs being in possession of the land of schedule 'A' has not been specifically denied by the non-contesting defendant Nos. 6-12 in their pleadings. The lone contesting defendant No.5 also in specific term has not denied the possession of the plaintiffs either in his pleading or in his deposition. From the side of the contesting defendants there is no evidence in denial of the claim of possession of the land described in schedule 'A' to the plaint by the plaintiffs. The fact of possession of the plaintiffs in the 'A' schedule land has been found on the basis of the evidence on record by the High Court Division as well as the court of appeal below. The learned Counsel for the petitioners has not been able to point out any infirmity in the finding of the High Court Division as well as of the court of appeal below relating to the possession of the land described in 'A' scheduled by the plaintiffs. The learned Counsel for the petitioners could also not point out any misreading of the evidence relating to the finding as to possession of the 'A' schedule land by the plaintiffs arrived at by the High Court Division and the court of appeal below. It has been submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioners that Exhibit 1 is a spurious document and that no ordinance should have been given to the same since the same was not endorsed by the then Pakistan High Commissioner in India and further, that Exhibit I was revalidated and re-stamped by the Office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla although property described in 'A' Schedule to Exhibit 1 is of the District of Noakhali. A registered document carries presumption of correctness of the endorsement made therein and that one who disputes the said presumption is under the law required to dislodge the correctness of the endorsement in the registered document. Exhibit I has been registered by the Munsif-cum-Magistrate of Udaypur, Tripura State, India. Since defendant No. 5 was disputing the genuineness of the registered document Exhibit 1 it was his duty to establish that there was nothing like Munsif Magistrate, Official or Office in Udaypur in the Tripura State who was authorized to register irrevocable power of attorney. But the said defendant totally failed to bring on record any material wherefrom it can said Munsif Magistrate, Udaypur, Tripura State, India was not competent to register Exhibit 1. The fact is that Exhibit 1 was revalidated and re-stamped by the Office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla. Official act has, the presumption of correctness and that one who challenges or disputes that presumption of correctness is required to establish that by legal evidence. From the defendants side nothing has been brought on record to show that Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue), Comilla was not the authorised officer for revalidating and re-stamping the document like Exhibit 1 relating to the property of the Zone ie Comilla-Noakhali, obtained by a migrant from India to then East Pakistan. Defendant No.1, the Government of Bangladesh, contested the suit by filing written statement and examining DW 1. DW 1 has not said anything about the incompetency or impropriety of re-validation and re-stamping of Exhibit 1 by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla, nor the witness has stated that at the relevant time document like Exhibit 1 wherein property of Noakhali as is being claimed by the migrant from India upon exchanging their property with the migrant from the then East Pakistan to India, the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Noakhali was vested with the authority to revalidate and re-stamp document like Exhibit 1. So, the contention of the learned Counsel for the petitioners that revalidating and re-stamping of Exhibit 1 by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla without noting the case number on initiation which the said revalidation and re-stamping was made is an element of forgery and collusiveness of the document is of no substance. The High Court Division as well as the court of Appeal below on examination and scrutiny of Exhibit 1 have arrived at the finding that the same is genuine since it has been registered by the Munsif Magistrate, Udaypur, Tripura State,. India and that revalidated and re- stamped by the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) Comilla upon affixing official seal and signing the name of the officer who re-stamped and revalidated the Exhibit 1. In Exhibit. 1 there is clear description of the properties ie properties described in the 'B' schedule to the plaint, which the plaintiff gave to the defendants in exchange of the properties as described in the schedule 'A' to the plaint of which defendants were the owners. So, it was the duty of the defendants to establish either that the property as described in schedule 'B' to the plaint are fictitious property or that although plaintiffs are claiming the said properties but, in fact, they did not own the said properties or they had no right, title and interest in the property as described in schedule 'B' to the plaint. The contesting defendant No.5 has not taken any step to establish that the properties described in the schedule 'B' to the plaint were not of the plaintiffs while denying the plaintiffs' claim of exchanging 'B' schedule land with the 'A' schedule land. The High Court Division as well as appellate Court have concurrently held that the plaintiffs are in possession of the 'A' schedule land. The defendants miserably failed to establish that plaintiffs on the basis of Exhibit 1 are not in possession of the 'A' schedule land. The moot point for consideration is that had there been no exchange then how the plaintiffs went into possession of the land when there is no allegation from the side of the defendants that plaintiffs entered into possession of the land forcibly upon dispossessing the defendants. In our view, upon total consideration of the facts and circumstance of the case and that particularly the factum of possession of the land in suit ie 'A' schedule land, by the plaintiffs, the High Court Division as well as the court of appeal below were in no way in error in arriving at the finding that by Exhibit 1 there was exchange of the properties between the parties as described in Schedule 'A' and 'B' to the plaint and that on the basis of the exchange as evidenced by the Exhibit 1, the plaintiffs went into possession of the 'A' schedule land in August 1963 and they are in possession of the land and that have acquired interest in the land in suit, The defendants although contended that Exhibit 1 is a spurious document but in support thereof have not brought any material on record, rather the High Court Division and the appellate Court on examination and scrutiny of Exhibit 1 have held that the same is a genuine document and that there is no internal or external infirmity as regard the document for considering the same as not genuine. 

 20. The plaintiffs went into possession of the plaint 'A' schedule land on the basis of Exhibit 1- irrevocable power of attorney in the form of deed of exchange and the said fact of obtaining of the possession of plaint 'A' schedule land on consideration of the legal evidence on record has been found genuine. The possession was obtained 39 years back from now and the plaintiffs are in uninterrupted possession of the land. Except contending by the defendant No.1 that recorded tenants left the then Pakistan for India and the land in plaint a schedule was declared evacuee property by notification of July 1965 and the said notification was published in the Gazette of November 4, 1965 no material worthy of consideration has been brought on record to establish the fact that property tall could be treated evacuee or enemy property because of the fact plaintiffs are being in possession of the land in plaint 'A' schedule on the basis of Exhibit 1 from August, 1963. The defendant No.1 has not taken any step to dislodge the legal presumption, because of the revalidation and re-stamping of the Irrevocable Power of Attorney in the form of deed of exchange by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Comilla upon affixing official seal and putting signature, of the Exhibit 1. By possessing the land in plaint 'A' schedule for 39 years past as of now upon obtaining the same on the basis of Exhibit 1, which has been found genuine by the High Court Division as well as by the appellate Court, the plaintiffs have acquired right and interest which cannot be said indefeasible or, in other words, right and interest as have accrued to the plaintiffs in the land described in plaint 'A' schedule is indefeasible and that for the protection thereof the suit as framed can very much be maintained.
